Iran's economy minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran was 'fully prepared' for the new sanctions and predicted 'another defeat' for Washington, telling state television that neither China nor Russia had accepted the measures and that other countries would resist them. The UAE, one of Iran's largest trading partners alongside China and Turkey, announced last week it was halting all trade and financial transactions with Tehran.

The International Maritime Organization confirmed 68 maritime incidents in the Gulf and neighbouring waters over the six months of the war, in which at least 20 workers were killed, 35 wounded and one is missing, mostly on tankers. The rate slowed to no casualties during the peace talks and returned to roughly one incident every 2.8 days after they collapsed.

Pakistan's interior minister said talks in Tehran had made 'significant progress', with Pakistan's military saying the meetings between army chief Asim Munir and the Iranian leadership covered preventing further escalation, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and expediting an end to the conflict. The characterisation is Islamabad's; Tehran has not issued a matching statement and no terms have been published.

The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control named Singapore-based Wellbred Capital, with trading arms in the UAE and Switzerland, among close to 60 companies, individuals and vessels designated over Iran links, citing ties to Iranian oil shipping figure Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said Beijing's cooperation with Iran is conducted within the framework of international law and 'should not be interfered with or disrupted', and that China would take 'all necessary measures' to safeguard its rights and interests after Washington widened sanctions.

The New York Times reported, citing an internal State Department document, that Washington is preparing to return Foreign Service officers to Middle East embassies evacuated before and during the war, including in Israel, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Oman, Iraq and Kuwait, possibly from this week. The report is not independently verified; the department said it 'continuously reviews' its security posture.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: The October ceasefire is holding, but the friction has shifted to the occupied West Bank, where a far-right lawmaker smashed a Palestinian memorial under army escort — an act the Israeli military itself called unauthorised and viewed with 'utmost severity', and which drew criticism from the foreign minister and opposition figures. Singapore joined the states calling planned settlement expansion illegal and urging a halt. On the Gaza boundary the kite dispute continues, with parents urged to keep children from flying them after Israel threatened 'forceful actions'; the military says the kites carried nothing dangerous. The wider regional shift remains Washington's removal of Syria from its state-sponsors-of-terrorism list after 47 years.

timeline.event: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers are killed by an explosion.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel rejects President Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza.
Palestinians are told to leave homes in the West Bank village of Qusra that Israeli settlers had besieged.
Israeli forces block activists attempting to deliver aid to Palestinian families besieged by settlers at Qusra.
US officials say Washington wants Netanyahu to publicly condemn the settler siege at Qusra. Netanyahu has not commented publicly.

Israeli airstrikes on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon kill at least 11 people, Lebanon's health ministry says, in the deadliest day since the June truce. Israel says the strikes targeted Hezbollah.
A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Israel rejects Turkey's move to seek an Interpol red notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla case, calling it a 'pathetic attempt' to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu calls President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'.
Former French and British ambassadors urge Paris and London to take joint action on the Palestinian territories, where violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank has surged since the Gaza war began.

Israel says it fired at a 'terrorist' in southern Syria; Syria's foreign ministry says an Israeli drone hit a civilian car near Beit Jinn, west of Damascus, calling it a 'blatant violation' of Syrian sovereignty. Syrian state TV reports one person injured. It is the second Israeli strike in Syria in a week, after the Abu al-Duhur airbase attack the US called an 'unnecessary escalation'.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Israeli military, Syrian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: The Straits Times reports that the widening confrontation between Israel and Turkey could reshape the region, with Syria - which physically separates the two - bearing the brunt of their rivalry.

Syria's government condemns the Israeli strike on the village of Beit Jinn, south-west of Damascus, as a violation of its sovereignty and of international law; officials say it hit a civilian vehicle and injured several people. The Israeli military says it targeted a 'terrorist' in the 'final stages' of preparing attacks posing an immediate threat to its soldiers.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Syrian officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack says the earlier Israeli strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase could be 'the Israelis baiting the Turks' in an attempt to draw Ankara into a conflict. Washington had already called that strike an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani says he expects security talks with Israel to resume soon despite an absence of trust, with Damascus seeking an Israeli withdrawal from Syrian land and an end to strikes. He says the US is pressing Israel to return to negotiations, and denies Syria allowed Turkish forces at the airbase Israel bombed this week.

Syria and Israel hold high-level US-mediated talks in Jordan, focused on practical mechanisms to halt Israeli strikes, arrests and targeted operations and on reviving negotiations towards a security agreement, Syria's state news agency SANA reports citing a diplomatic source. Israel's prime minister's office did not comment.

At the Jordan talks, Damascus says its immediate priorities remain an Israeli withdrawal to positions held before Bashar al-Assad's overthrow on 8 Dec 2024 and full restoration of the 1974 disengagement agreement, and that it will not accept limits on rebuilding its armed forces, according to SANA.

Syrian state news agency SANA reports that Syria and Israel held further US-mediated talks aimed at easing tensions, following the round held in Jordan on 23 August. Israel's prime minister's office has not commented.

Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz warned of 'forceful actions' after four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, about 800m from the Gaza boundary, and several more elsewhere in southern Israel. The Israeli military said the kites carried no suspicious materials and posed no threat. Hamas denied responsibility, called them 'basically children's toys from displacement camps', and accused Israel of using them as a pretext for continued strikes despite the ceasefire agreed last October.
Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked a ship off Saudi Arabia's Yanbu. There was no Saudi confirmation of the claim.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli fire killed two young children. The account comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, and removed Hayat Tahrir al-Sham from its list of global terrorist organisations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it recognised Damascus distancing itself from international terrorism; Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani called it a 'historic step'. Syria remains at the centre of tension between Israel and Turkey.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Syria 'shakes off a dark stain and tears away a painful chapter of its past' after the US removed the country from its state-sponsors-of-terrorism list, thanking President Trump. The Treasury announced corresponding sanctions relief; Hayat Tahrir al-Sham was also delisted as a global terrorist organisation.

Far-right Israeli lawmaker and settler activist Zvi Sukkot took a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in Madama in the northern occupied West Bank while under military escort. The army said the demolition was unauthorised and a misuse of security protection, that soldiers stopped it and removed him, and that it viewed the incident with 'utmost severity'; Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot also criticised him.

Parents in Gaza were urged to stop children flying kites after Israel's warning to Hamas over kites found near the boundary. Israel's defence minister had threatened 'forceful actions'; the Israeli military says the kites carried nothing dangerous and Hamas calls them children's toys.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: The DRC's Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic keeps outrunning WHO's formal paperwork — ECDC's running count sits more than 800 confirmed cases ahead of the last Disease Outbreak News, published a fortnight ago, with the case-fatality ratio still near half. US measles added more than 200 cases in a single week, double the week before, and has already passed last year's post-elimination record. Europe's West Nile season is quieter but still adding newly affected areas each week. For readers the practical steps are unglamorous: check measles vaccination before travelling, and use repellent in southern Europe.

outbreaks.name: DR Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: Public health emergency of international concern; still expanding, case-fatality ratio near 48%
outbreaks.scope_note: DR Congo confirmed cases and confirmed deaths only, re-read from ECDC's outbreak page on 25 Aug: the page was last updated 24 Aug 15:41 and reports DRC data up to 22 Aug (55 new cases and 36 deaths since the 21 Aug report). 808 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 1,200 have recovered; Ituri is worst hit with 4,607 cases and 2,065 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones. Uganda reported 20 confirmed cases and two deaths and declared its outbreak over on 28 Jul; single imported cases were treated in Germany and France, which is why the country count is three. WHO's latest formal Disease Outbreak News (DON615, 14 Aug) counted 4,686 confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths across all countries as of 12 Aug — the newer ECDC/DRC figures are not yet DON-ratified.

outbreaks.name: United States — measles
outbreaks.status: Accelerating; 2026 has already passed 2025's post-1991 record
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed US cases in calendar 2026 as of the CDC's 20 Aug weekly update, re-checked on 25 Aug: 211 cases were added in that single week, more than double the 101 added the week before, and 36 outbreaks have been reported this year. No measles deaths have been recorded in 2026, against three in 2025. All of 2025 saw 2,289 cases, the highest annual total since 1991 until this year overtook it. The CDC measles data page returned HTTP 403 to this run, so the figures come from CIDRAP's report of the CDC weekly update; no newer CDC update had been published by the evening of 25 Aug.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus (2026 season)
outbreaks.status: Peak transmission season; new areas still being added weekly
outbreaks.scope_note: Locally acquired human cases reported to ECDC for the 2026 transmission season, re-read on 25 Aug from the weekly overview produced on 21 Aug: Italy 311, Greece 157 (seven with unknown place of infection), Spain 63, North Macedonia 37, Romania 28, France 17, Serbia 6, the Netherlands 2, and one each in Albania, Austria, Germany and Kosovo. Twenty-one areas were reported as affected for the first time this season in that week, six of them for the first time ever. ECDC's weekly overview is a blood-safety product and publishes no consolidated death count, so deaths are shown as unavailable rather than zero. No week-35 update had been published by the evening of 25 Aug.

stories.headline: ECDC's running count puts the DRC Ebola epidemic at 5,514 confirmed cases and 2,642 deaths
stories.summary: ECDC's outbreak page, last updated on 24 August, reports 5,514 confirmed cases and 2,642 deaths in DR Congo from data up to 22 August — an increase of 55 cases and 36 deaths on the previous day's report. Ituri accounts for 4,607 cases and 2,065 deaths. A total of 808 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 1,200 have recovered, and 83.4% of identified contacts are under follow-up. ECDC notes DRC's figures are under continuous review and harmonisation.

stories.headline: WHO's latest formal outbreak notice counts 4,686 confirmed Ebola cases as of 12 August
stories.summary: Disease Outbreak News 615, published on 14 August, is WHO's most recent formal notice: 4,686 confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths across all affected countries as of 12 August, of which 4,665 cases and 2,184 deaths were in DR Congo, for a case-fatality ratio of 46.8%. That is already the largest Ebola outbreak documented in the country, ahead of the 3,317 cases of 2018-2020. The newer national and ECDC counts run well ahead of this and are not yet DON-ratified.

stories.headline: CDC adds 211 measles cases in a week as the US total reaches 2,777
stories.summary: The CDC's weekly update on 20 August added 211 confirmed cases, more than double the 101 added the week before, taking the 2026 US total to 2,777 across 36 reported outbreaks. No deaths have been recorded this year, against three in 2025. The total has already passed the 2,289 cases recorded in all of 2025, which was itself the highest since 1991.

stories.headline: ECDC counts 625 locally acquired West Nile cases across 12 European countries
stories.summary: ECDC's weekly overview produced on 21 August reports 625 locally acquired human West Nile cases this season, led by Italy with 311 and Greece with 157. Twenty-one areas were reported affected for the first time this season that week, and six regions recorded locally acquired cases for the first time ever, including Pyrenees-Orientales in France and Rhein-Pfalz-Kreis in Germany.

stories.headline: ECDC's week-34 threats report keeps Ebola and West Nile on the watchlist
stories.summary: The Communicable Disease Threats Report for 15-21 August continues to list the DRC Ebola outbreak and the European West Nile season among the threats ECDC is actively monitoring. The report's detailed figures sit in its PDF, so it is used here as a dated corroborator rather than a source of headline counts.

stories.headline: Louisiana girl, 8, dies from a rare brain-eating amoeba after swimming in a lake
stories.summary: An eight-year-old girl in Louisiana died after contracting Naegleria fowleri, the amoeba that causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, following a swim in a lake. Infections are extremely rare but almost always fatal; US health authorities advise holding the nose or using nose clips when jumping into warm fresh water.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Shadowserver now counts more than 270 Zimbra servers compromised through CVE-2026-73570, the SNMP command-injection flaw CISA gave federal agencies just three days to fix — and roughly 8,200 unpatched instances are still exposed. The patch queue behind it is heavy: a maximum-severity Oracle WebLogic proxy plug-in flaw is being exploited in the wild, and a Keycloak reset-credentials bug lets an unauthenticated attacker take over any account on an identity provider. Credential theft is the other theme of the cycle, from a phishing kit that harvested thousands of Microsoft 365 sessions after users completed MFA normally to npm packages quietly serving fake CAPTCHA pages from a trusted CDN. Patch Zimbra, WebLogic and Keycloak first; treat MFA-completed session theft as the reason to move towards phishing-resistant sign-in.

stories.headline: More than 270 Zimbra servers already breached through the actively exploited SNMP flaw
stories.summary: Shadowserver has now identified more than 270 compromised Zimbra Collaboration Suite instances as of 22 August, against roughly 8,200 unpatched servers still exposed. The flaw is a command injection in the optional zimbra-snmp package: with SNMP notifications enabled, an unauthenticated attacker can send crafted requests that execute arbitrary OS commands as the zimbra user. NVD scores it 8.9. CERT Polska first flagged exploitation on 21 August; CISA added it to the KEV catalogue the same day with an unusually short three-day federal deadline of 24 August. The fix shipped in ZCS 10.1.20 on 20 July.

stories.headline: Mirage2FA phishing-as-a-service harvested Microsoft 365 sessions from thousands of companies
stories.summary: Researchers tracking the Mirage2FA (LinXcoded) platform report it targeted 9,426 unique email addresses and potentially compromised 4,532 of them — roughly a 48% success rate — across US and EU organisations, with about 64% of identified victims in the United States and technology, manufacturing and education most affected. It is an adversary-in-the-middle kit: business-themed lures carry an HTML attachment that uses HTML smuggling and obfuscated JavaScript to render a Microsoft-branded login page, lets the user complete MFA normally, then steals the authenticated session cookie. MFA alone does not stop this; phishing-resistant authentication and conditional-access token binding do.
stories.source: The Hacker News, ANY.RUN, Help Net Security

stories.headline: 24 npm packages abuse unpkg mirrors to host fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA pages
stories.summary: The packages contain no malicious install script — each is essentially a single HTML page. The trick is that npm CDN mirrors such as unpkg render that page live from a trusted domain, giving attackers free, reputable hosting for ClickFix-style fake Cloudflare verification pages. The redirect logic currently sends visitors to a legitimate site, but it is remotely controlled and can be repointed at phishing or ClickFix infrastructure at any time. Some of the packages were still downloadable at the time of reporting. It follows the 2025 Beamglea campaign, which used 175 npm packages on the same CDN for credential harvesting — worth adding unpkg-hosted HTML to web-proxy review rather than treating the domain as inherently safe.

stories.headline: E4del and PINHOLE RATs turn FTP server banners into dead-drop resolvers
stories.summary: SOCRadar's threat research unit says attackers have been hiding command-and-control instructions in the greeting banner an FTP server returns on connection, a technique seen in the wild since early July and still operating with new infrastructure in August. It led to two previously undocumented remote-access trojans: E4del, a modular Node.js RAT packaged inside a digitally signed Electron app masquerading as Discord, with eight commands including live desktop streaming; and PINHOLE, a multi-stage RAT with fourteen command types that pulls its C2 from Pinterest and SurveyMonkey behind Cloudflare Workers. Infection starts from a ZIP archive with an LNK chain, likely delivered by phishing. Outbound FTP from workstations is the detection opportunity.

stories.headline: Interpol's Operation Jackal IV nets 58 arrests across 22 countries
stories.summary: Interpol said the operation, which ran from November 2025 to June 2026 against West African organised crime networks including the Black Axe syndicate, led to 58 arrests and identified 263 suspects across 22 participating countries — 39 arrests in South Africa, 17 in Argentina and 11 in Romania. Investigators blocked 257 bank accounts and seized about US$2.67 million, and linked 196 suspects to a crime-as-a-service network supplying domains and money-laundering support for romance scams, investment fraud, business email compromise and sextortion.

stories.headline: Actively exploited Oracle WebLogic proxy plug-in flaw carries a maximum CVSS 10.0
stories.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-21962 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 24 August, confirming attacks in the wild. NVD scores it 10.0 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C) — an easily exploitable flaw in the WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in for Apache HTTP Server and IIS that lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access over HTTP compromise the product and read critical data. Affected supported versions are Oracle Fusion Middleware 12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0 and 14.1.2.0.0. Patch or remove the plug-in now.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: Unpatched Calix router flaw lets unauthenticated attackers punch holes through the NAT
stories.summary: A UPnP weakness in the Calix GS7 XGS (model GS5239XG, also sold as GigaSpire 7u10txg) on EXOS/6.6.47 lets remote, unauthenticated attackers create arbitrary port-forwarding rules, delete or enumerate existing mappings and read the router's public IP — exposing devices behind the NAT directly to the internet. No patch is available: the researcher's attempt to reach the vendor on 7 June went unanswered, prompting coordinated disclosure through CERT/CC. The workaround is to disable UPnP under Advanced → Security, though some ISPs lock that setting.

stories.headline: WordPress sites under active attack through a miniOrange SAML SSO authentication bypass
stories.summary: Two flaws in the miniOrange SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On plugin allow authentication bypass across seven editions — free before 5.4.5, premium before 13.0.4, standard before 17.06, premium/enterprise/all-inclusive multisite before 20.2.8, enterprise/all-inclusive before 26.0.3, VIP before 32.0.8 and VIP multisite before 35.0.7. BleepingComputer reports exploitation attempts and opportunistic scanning already underway from six IP addresses across Europe, Africa and the US, with a public proof-of-concept for the free edition. The vendor puts its customer base across the family at about 30,000.

stories.headline: TikTok agrees to a US$400 million settlement over US children's privacy claims
stories.summary: TikTok will pay US$400 million to settle a US lawsuit alleging violations of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act. Nothing to patch, but it resets the compliance baseline for anyone handling under-13 user data at scale.

stories.headline: Weedhack malware spreads through fake Minecraft clients and SEO poisoning
stories.summary: The Hacker News reports a malware-as-a-service operation distributing itself as cracked or cheat Minecraft clients, pushed to the top of search results through SEO poisoning. The lure targets a young, game-focused audience that is likely to disable antivirus to run a "cheat" binary — worth flagging to households and school networks rather than enterprise fleets.

stories.headline: ReliaQuest says a ShinyHunters phishing attack got a foothold but stole nothing
stories.summary: The security vendor confirmed that attackers impersonating its own security staff stood up a lookalike domain, reliaquest.claims, behind a CDN and phished an employee, who entered credentials on a fake single sign-on portal and approved the MFA prompt. That gave view-only access to an identity dashboard; device-trust controls blocked everything after that, and ReliaQuest says no applications, systems or customer data were touched. ShinyHunters has been registering .claims domains to impersonate company help desks — a pattern worth adding to domain-monitoring rules.

stories.headline: Hard-coded encryption key exposes 5,000 applicants on a South Korean government startup platform
stories.summary: Modu-ui Changup, a startup support platform overseen by South Korea's Ministry of SMEs and Startups, encrypted applicant data but shipped the encryption key inside the API itself. Attackers using ordinary web-crawling techniques retrieved the ciphertext and the key together, exposing email addresses, evaluation comments and startup idea summaries for roughly 5,000 successful applicants. A textbook reminder that encryption buys nothing if the key sits beside the data.

stories.headline: Microsoft's August updates break printing and PDF export in WPF applications
stories.summary: Microsoft confirmed that this month's Windows updates break printing and PDF export in applications built on Windows Presentation Foundation. Relevant to anyone weighing how fast to roll August's cumulative update across an estate — the security fixes still need to go on, but line-of-business WPF apps should be tested first.

stories.headline: WordlistLoader delivers Amatera Stealer via ClickFix while SynkLoader phishes Windows passwords
stories.summary: The Hacker News details two loaders running in parallel: WordlistLoader, delivered through ClickFix-style fake verification pages, which drops the Amatera infostealer; and SynkLoader, which prompts users for their Windows password. BleepingComputer separately tracked SynkLoader being pushed through a Microsoft Teams phishing campaign. Both rely on the user pasting or typing something themselves, so user-facing warnings about "paste this to verify" prompts are the practical control.

stories.headline: Critical Keycloak flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker reset any account's password
stories.summary: A flaw in the reset-credentials flow of the keycloak-services component — the core engine of Red Hat Build of Keycloak — allows an unauthenticated attacker to take over any account, NVD scoring it 9.1. Keycloak sits in front of internal applications at a great many organisations, so a full account takeover here is an identity-provider compromise, not a single-app one. Two further Keycloak issues were published the same week: CVE-2026-15571 (7.3, legacy client-initiated account-linking endpoint) and CVE-2026-19608 (5.3, group policy provider).

stories.headline: Operation QUICSILVER hits Myanmar's government and IT sector with a QUIC-tunnelling backdoor
stories.summary: The Hacker News reports a campaign against Myanmar government bodies and IT providers deploying a backdoor dubbed QUICAgent, which tunnels its command-and-control traffic over the QUIC protocol. QUIC rides on UDP/443 and is frequently waved through by egress filtering built for TCP, so defenders who cannot inspect it should at least be alerting on unexpected UDP/443 to non-CDN destinations.

stories.headline: UAT-10147 pairs an AI-assisted Linux rootkit with BYOVD EDR bypass to scale up server attacks
stories.summary: The Hacker News reports a threat cluster tracked as UAT-10147 using AI to scale its server-attack workflow and deploying an implant called SPECTRE, combining a Linux rootkit with an EDR bypass. Server estates without kernel-level monitoring — especially internet-facing Linux hosts — are the exposure here.

stories.headline: ToxicPanda 2.0 abuses Android VPN permissions to cut phones off from Google Play
stories.summary: A new version of the ToxicPanda Android banking trojan requests VPN permissions and uses them to block traffic to Google Play, keeping Play Protect from updating or removing it. Users who cannot reach the Play Store on an Android device should treat that as a possible indicator rather than a network glitch.

stories.headline: Android car head units conscripted into a proxy botnet
stories.summary: BleepingComputer reports Android-based aftermarket car head units shipping with, or being infected by, malware that turns them into residential proxy nodes for other people's traffic. An awkward class of device: rarely patched, rarely monitored, and sitting on whatever Wi-Fi or tethered connection the owner gives it.
